## THE PLATFORM PROBE IS UP — Gerrit 1320, and it settles AC1 without depending on any rebar path

Two helpers in `_dc_support.py`, wired into BOTH sub-task parent cells (outbound and inbound):
 * `probe_subtask_parent_put(dc_request, key, new_parent, *, verb="fields"|"update")` — a raw REST
   PUT bypassing pycontribs entirely, capturing the HTTP status and body `dc_transport.set_parent`
   never surfaces;
 * `probe_subtask_parent_editmeta_ops(dc_request, key)` — reads which operations DC actually exposes
   on `parent`, one of the two falsifiers recorded on [rebar:37e7-d751-0042-4b94].

Both verb forms are probed, which is the other falsifier: if `{"update":{"parent":[{"set":…}]}}`
behaves differently from `{"fields":{"parent":…}}`, the NOT-RESOLVABLE verdict on 37e7 is wrong.

**AC1 becomes answerable from the run output alone:** a 2xx with an unchanged read-back is
accept-and-ignore; a 4xx is rejection. Neither depends on rebar code being correct.

The probes deliberately DO NOT assert on their own — their results fold into the existing oracles'
failure messages, so they add diagnosis without adding a new way for the suite to go red.

Design note: the update-verb example recorded on this ticket was for the CLEAR case, but the wiring
target is the SET case; the helper was generalised to build `{"set": {"key": …}}` when reparenting
and `{"set": None}` when clearing, so one helper covers both.

Verified on current `gerrit/main`: hygiene 0, ruff clean, mypy 421, 58 live tests collect (unchanged).
